source.title: Antidote: Post-fine-tuning Safety Alignment for Large Language Models against Harmful Fine-tuning
source.authors: Tian-Sheng Huang; Gautam Bhattacharya; Pratik Joshi; J. Kimball; Ling Liu

record.tranche_reason: The study measures harmful outputs after harmful-data fine-tuning and benign-data fine-tuning, bearing directly on safety degradation, but uses its own datasets, settings, and harmful-score evaluation rather than reporting an explicit replication of the original method.
record.gate_note: The paper reports harmful scores for fine-tuned models and post-fine-tuning defenses. Harmful score is the percentage of outputs flagged unsafe by the BeaverTails moderation model on 1000 harmful instructions; it is not a refusal-rate measure. Rows below prioritize SFT attack results, selected post-pruning results, benign fine-tuning, model comparisons, and the pruning-ratio results relevant to weight localization. Accuracy results are not separate rows because they do not measure the claim’s safety behavior.
record.test_reason: This is mainly a defense paper, but its undefended SFT baseline shows harmful score rising with harmful data. Clean fine-tuning scores 52.3; 5% harmful data gives 76.7 (Table 1). With refusal-data alignment, the clean score is 13.5 and 5% harmful gives 80.3 (Table 7). The method differs from the originals: LoRA, self-aligned base models, harmful data mixed into task data, and a BeaverTails moderation score.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that existing alignment-stage and fine-tuning-stage defenses against harmful fine-tuning fail at large learning rates or many epochs. They propose Antidote, one-shot pruning of weights important to harmful data after fine-tuning, which they say cuts harmful score while keeping downstream accuracy. They also claim Antidote handles benign fine-tuning attacks. They treat harmful fine-tuning breaking alignment as an established premise, not a finding of their own.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses safety-aligned models followed by fine-tuning with harmful data mixed into downstream-task data, and evaluates unsafe outputs with a moderation model. It also tests benign fine-tuning and adds post-fine-tuning pruning; it is not presented as an explicit replication of either named original source.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported outcomes vary with harmful-data ratio, fine-tuning sample count, learning rate, epoch count, downstream dataset, backbone model, and Antidote mask ratio.

fits_no_version.finding: Random pruning of a model fine-tuned on benign GSM8K data lowers harmful score about as much as Antidote's targeted pruning (57.4 vs 57.1, from 61.5). Random pruning cuts accuracy more (14.9 vs 27.8).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In fine-tuned models, the drop in harmful score after pruning may not be specific to weights identified as harmful.

fits_no_version.finding: In Antidote pruning, a larger mask ratio lowers both harmful score and fine-tune accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Post-fine-tuning pruning trades harmfulness for task accuracy.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning; Proceedings of the 42nd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 267 (2025)
record.problems: Harmful score is a moderation-model unsafe-output rate rather than a refusal rate. The clean condition in Table 1 already has a harmful score of 52.30. The benign-fine-tuning table gives no matched no-fine-tuning reference. No uncertainty estimates are reported.
record.rows_left_out: At most 60 rows were allowed. Excluded detailed harmful-score results for RepNoise, Vaccine, Lisa, and LDIFS in Tables 1–4; Antidote sample-count results in Table 2; results for the additional downstream datasets and alignment-data condition in Tables 6–7; and the Llama3-8B result in Table 9. These are additional defense or dataset/model results; the retained rows cover direct SFT attack outcomes and major variation conditions. Table 11 accuracy values were omitted because they are not safety-behavior measures. Other reported results, including HED and output-logit drift, do not measure the versions’ named behaviors.

untested.parts: Harmful-only fine-tuning of production safety-tuned chat models (e.g. Llama-2-chat), full-parameter fine-tuning, and refusal-rate measures. The models here are self-aligned with LoRA on BeaverTails safe data, and the default alignment leaves a clean harmful score of about 52%.
Whether benign data raises harmful compliance. No pre-fine-tuning aligned-model harmful score is reported, so the size of any increase is unknown.
Not tested: no per-token KL or position analysis.
Not tested: no prefilling, suffix or decoding attacks.
Not tested on aligned models. Pruning is applied to fine-tuned models to remove harmful behaviour, not to locate safety.

missing.what: SFT harmful score with BeaverTails-refusal safety alignment: 13.5 clean vs 80.3/78.8/78.6/82.3 at p=0.05/0.1/0.2/0.5. This is the strongest V1 evidence, because it starts from a well-aligned baseline.
SFT harmful score across fine-tuning datasets at p=0.2: SST2 79.4, AGNEWS 79.6, GSM8K 77.8, AlpacaEval 73.8.
Llama3-8B SFT harmful score; the values are not readable in the extracted text.

record.verdict_notes: This is a defense paper; V1 evidence comes only from the undefended SFT baseline. The default alignment is weak: 52.3% of outputs are already unsafe after clean fine-tuning, so increases sit on a high floor. Table 7 (refusal-data alignment) is the cleaner test and should be added as rows. Rows for the study's own method and the defense comparators were relinked to none. The record's V2 limits_scope label is dropped: a missing baseline makes the result undeterminable, not scope-limiting. Harmful score comes from the BeaverTails moderation model, not a refusal rate.

versions.untested_parts: The study reports harmful-score rates after harmful-data fine-tuning, not refusal rates. It tests mixed harmful/downstream data and a sample-count sweep, but not all few-to-hundreds-example recipes or harmful-only fine-tuning.

The benign fine-tuning experiment reports post-fine-tuning harmful scores but does not provide a matched aligned, un-fine-tuned harmful-score reference in that table; it therefore does not establish the size of an increase.
No aligned-versus-base per-token KL or response-position analysis.
No compliant-opening prefills, suffix attacks, or decoding changes are tested.
The study prunes high-scoring coordinates in an already fine-tuned model; it does not test whether safety behavior in an aligned model is localized in a small set of weights or ranks.
No test of why safety is shallow or of the data/objective as a cause of shallowness.
No training intended to spread safety beyond the first response tokens, or test of whether such deepening holds up.

relationships.condition: Undefended SFT on self-aligned Llama2/Mistral/Gemma-7B, harmful data mixed into task data at 5–50%, default lr 1e-4, 1–40 epochs
relationships.reason: Harmful score rises from 52.3 clean to 76.7–80.2 with harmful data (T1-SFT-p005..p05). It stays at about 77–81 across sample counts ≥1000, epochs and models (T2-SFT-n1000..n5000, T4-SFT-*, T8-*-SFT). The refusal-alignment variant (13.5→80.3) is in the text only, not the rows.
relationships.display_finding: Harmful score rose from 52.3 with clean data to 76.7–80.2 with harmful data. It stayed around 77–81 with 1000 or more samples, across epoch settings and across models. A refusal-aligned variant went from 13.5 to 80.3.

relationships.condition: Very small learning rate (1e-7) or very few harmful examples (n=100, about 20 harmful)
relationships.reason: At lr=1e-7 the score stays at the clean level, 52.8 (T3-SFT-lr1e7). With about 20 harmful examples the rise is smaller, to 65.5 (T2-SFT-n100). The effect depends on fine-tuning strength.
relationships.display_finding: At learning rate 1e-7 the harmful score stayed at the clean level of 52.8, and with about 20 harmful examples it rose only to 65.5, so the effect depends on fine-tuning strength.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
